title: A single injective complex gives compatible derived section models on slice sites
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site in a fixed coefficient universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], $\Lambda$ a unital ring, and $\Lambda_{\mathcal C}$ its constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use left-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For each object $W$, give $\mathcal C/W$ the localized topology and restrict sheaves sectionwise as in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]; its terminal object is $\operatorname{id}_W$. Restriction identifies the restricted constant ring sheaf with the constant $\Lambda$-ring sheaf of the slice. Let $L^\bullet$ be a bounded-below complex of injective $\Lambda_{\mathcal C}$-module sheaves [def-sp-injective-resolutions], let $K\in D^+(\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_{\mathcal C}))$, and fix $e:QL^\bullet\cong K$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Restriction to every slice is exact and preserves injective module sheaves. There are canonical isomorphisms in $D^+(\Lambda\text{-}\operatorname{Mod})$
$$\alpha_W:Q(L^\bullet(W))\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(\mathcal C/W,K|_W).$$
Here $L^\bullet(W)$ has the actual evaluation differential. For every arrow $a:W'\to W$, let $r_a$ be the degreewise sheaf restriction $L^\bullet(W)\to L^\bullet(W')$, and let $\rho_a$ be canonical derived section pullback along the localization $\mathcal C/W'\to\mathcal C/W$, with the sectionwise identification $(K|_W)|_{W'}=K|_{W'}$. Then
$$\rho_a\circ\alpha_W=\alpha_{W'}\circ Q(r_a).$$
The isomorphisms are natural in maps of the specified complexes and their identifications $e$. Consequently, for any small category $I$ and diagram $D:I\to\mathcal C$, the literal section complexes $L^\bullet(D(i))$ form a strict $I^{\mathrm{op}}$-diagram, with one lower bound, representing these derived section objects and their canonical transition maps. For an injective module sheaf $J$, each $J|_W$ has zero positive module cohomology on the slice.

proof.text: Put $S_W(F)=F|_W$. By [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], $S_W(F)(V\to W)=F(V)$, with the original restriction maps, and $\operatorname{id}_W$ is terminal. The localization inverse image on sheaves of sets is this sectionwise restriction; [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] identifies its pullback of $\Lambda_{\mathcal C}$ with $\Lambda_{\mathcal C/W}$ and says that the resulting left-module inverse image is exact, including for noncommutative $\Lambda$. It is precisely $S_W$: the addition and scalar action at $V\to W$ are those of $F(V)$. In particular it sends a zero map to zero, preserves quasi-isomorphisms termwise and induces the stated restriction of derived objects. Applying [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] inside $\mathcal C/W$ gives $S_a S_W=S_{W'}$ sectionwise for $a:W'\to W$.

source.place: Tag 04IX, definition-localize-ringed-site; Tag 03DH, section-localize; relocalization and constant coefficients

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized-adjunction] to the ring sheaf $\Lambda_{\mathcal C}$ and $W$; the zero-map hypothesis holds by step 1. It supplies $G_W\dashv S_W$ with $G_W$ preserving finite limits and finite colimits, hence exact. The module-sheaf categories are abelian by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Therefore [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives], with exact left adjoint $G_W$ and right adjoint $S_W$, proves that $S_W$ preserves injective objects. This also applies on every slice, so $S_a$ preserves injectives. For the given $L$, every $S_WL$ is thus a bounded-below complex of injectives with the same lower bound: if $L^n=0$, then $(S_WL)^n(V\to W)=0$ for every test object.

source.place: Tag 03F3, lemma-cohomology-of-open (1), proof using exact extension by zero (03DI–03DJ) and Homology 015Z

proof.text:
All sites and coefficients lie in the fixed universe, and each slice of the small site is small. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] and [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives], their left-module-sheaf categories have enough injectives. The target $\Lambda\text{-}\operatorname{Mod}$ is abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-enough-injectives]. For a slice let $E_W(F)=F(\operatorname{id}_W)$, regarded as a left $\Lambda$-module by constant scalars. It is additive since evaluation preserves addition of morphisms. It is left exact since kernels are sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] to $E_W$. Denote its derived functor by $RE_W=R\Gamma(\mathcal C/W,-)$ and its natural unit by $\eta^W_M:Q(E_WM)\to RE_W(QM)$. The unit is invertible on bounded-below complexes of injectives. Step 2 and the sectionwise definition give $E_W(S_WL)=L(W)$ as complexes: the differential in degree $n$ is exactly $(d_L^n)_W$. Define
$$\alpha_W=RE_W(S_We)\circ\eta^W_{S_WL}.$$
Both factors are isomorphisms, with target $RE_W(S_WK)$, as required.

Fix $a:W'\to W$ and work on $\mathcal C/W$. For a module sheaf $F$ there is the natural section restriction $t_a(F):E_WF\to E_{W'}S_aF$, evaluated on the arrow $(W'\xrightarrow a W)\to\operatorname{id}_W$. It is $\Lambda$-linear, and for complexes it commutes with the differential by naturality of $d$. By the universal property (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], the transformation on bounded-below complexes
$$Q(E_WM)\xrightarrow{Q(t_a(M))}Q(E_{W'}S_aM)\xrightarrow{\eta^{W'}_{S_aM}}RE_{W'}(Q(S_aM))$$
extends uniquely across the unit $\eta^W$ to a transformation $\rho_a:RE_W\to RE_{W'}S_a^D$, where $S_a^D$ is induced by exact restriction. This is canonical derived section pullback: it derives the ordinary section pullback along localization, and uniqueness specifies its normalization. Its defining equality is
$$\rho_{a,QM}\circ\eta^W_M=\eta^{W'}_{S_aM}\circ Q(t_a(M)).$$
For $M=S_WL$, relocalization [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] identifies $S_aM=S_{W'}L$ sectionwise, while $t_a(M)$ is literally $r_a$. Thus the equality uses the actual evaluation differential and actual restriction map, rather than a chosen map between isomorphic cohomology objects.

source.place: Tag 03F3 and equation-restriction-mapping immediately following it; derived.tex Tags 05S9–05SA, derived-functor unit universal property

proof.text:
Naturality of $\rho_a$ at $S_We:Q(S_WL)\cong S_WK$ gives
$$\rho_{a,S_WK}\,RE_W(S_We)=RE_{W'}(S_{W'}e)\,\rho_{a,Q(S_WL)}.$$
Compose this with $\eta^W_{S_WL}$ and substitute step 4. The result is exactly $\rho_a\alpha_W=\alpha_{W'}Q(r_a)$. For a chain map $f:L\to L'$ and a derived map $u:K\to K'$ satisfying $u e=e'Q(f)$, naturality of the unit from [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] gives
$$RE_W(S_Wu)\alpha_W=\alpha'_W Q(f(W)).$$
This proves naturality for the specified representatives and identifications, including changes of $e$. The only identities used are naturality and composition of the displayed functors.

source.place: Tag 05SA, lemma-derived-functor, naturality of the derived-functor unit; sites-cohomology.tex equation-restriction-mapping

proof.text: For $D:I\to\mathcal C$, evaluation of the presheaves underlying $L^n$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] gives $L^n(D(\operatorname{id}_i))=\operatorname{id}$ and $L^n(D(b\circ a))=L^n(D(a))\circ L^n(D(b))$. These equalities hold in each degree; naturality of $d_L$ makes every restriction a chain map. Hence the literal complexes form a strict $I^{\mathrm{op}}$-diagram. If $L^n=0$ for $n<N$, every complex in that diagram is zero below $N$. Steps 3–5 identify its objects and arrows with the specified derived section objects and canonical transitions. Finally take an injective sheaf $J$ in degree zero. Step 2 makes $S_WJ[0]$ a bounded-below injective complex. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] its module derived sections are $Q(J(W)[0])$, whose cohomology in every positive degree is zero. This is the last assertion, without any assertion that the underlying abelian sheaf of $J$ is injective.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q143-0c0f078d4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item's six steps in full, the statements of all 15 cited nodes, the parent det-sf-comparison-affine-continuity (its Step 5 is the only citer), unit sk-prop-sf-comparison (uses []), Stacks 03F3 and its proof in sites-cohomology.tex, and Mathlib RightDerivedFunctorPlus.lean:36-55 and DerivabilityStructureInjectives.lean:376. Statement unchanged and no new nodes. Step 1: def-pur-localized-ringed-site gives sectionwise restriction and relocalization; lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image covers noncommutative Λ and gives exactness. Step 2 follows Stacks' own proof of 03F3(1): the extension-by-zero adjunction (zero-map hypothesis checked) plus right-adjoint-preserves-injectives in the right orientation. Step 3: enough injectives from the Grothendieck-abelian node on small slices; the right-derived-plus-injective hypotheses (abelian categories, enough injectives, additive evaluation through Λ→Λ_{C/W}(id_W)) hold; α_W = RE_W(S_W e)∘η is an isomorphism. Step 4: ρ_a comes from one application of the leaf's universal property (the transformation is natural on K^+, and t_a = r_a on S_W L), so marking it elementary is fair. Step 5: I recomputed the square ρ_aα_W = α_{W'}Q(r_a) and the naturality in (L,e); both are correct. Step 6: strict I^op diagram with one lower bound, and injective acyclicity via clause (2) without assuming that forgetting scalars preserves injectives. Edge cases: identity and terminal W, composable arrows, L=0, empty I, a lower bound N≠0, the zero ring, M_2(k). Coefficients are left modules over the constant ring sheaf, as in the parent; no SGA. Accepted tool_uses: lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized-adjunction (generic extension by zero) and lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck (generic, Lean-closed in slopmaster2).
